3D Texture Proxy Geometry is a GPU-accelerated volume rendering technique where the volumetric dataset is uploaded as a 3D texture object, and polygonal slices are rasterized and blended back-to-front to form the final image [S1, S2].

The claim states that 3D Texture Proxy Geometry is a GPU-accelerated volume rendering technique where the volumetric dataset is uploaded as a 3D texture object, and polygonal slices are rasterized and blended back-to-front to form the final image. Source [S1] explicitly describes '3D texture mapping' (a term often used interchangeably with or as the basis for proxy geometry techniques in this context) as a technique where the volume is uploaded as a 3D texture to the graphics card, and the GPU rasterizes polygonal slices through the volume parallel to the viewpoint, blending them in back-to-front order. Source [S2] corroborates this by describing 3D texture-based volume rendering on GPU using view-port aligned slices (polygons) cut from the 3D texture object, accessed via fragment programs (rasterization) after vertex processing. The core mechanism described in the claim matches the evidence provided in both sources.
